title: The Save
coreMove: Transfer checklist discipline to another field by rebuilding it around that field's recurring failure points.
sourcePressure: The source turns to investing and Mohnish Pabrai to show checklist logic beyond surgery, while keeping the lesson tied to practical routine discipline rather than generic business process.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says checklists work everywhere. The real chapter says the logic transfers only when rebuilt around a domain's real failure modes.

sourceAnchors.name: Mohnish Pabrai
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar names Mohnish Pabrai as the anchor for checklist logic beyond medicine.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: Mohnish Pabrai matters because investing turns the checklist from a surgical tool into a guard against repeated judgment errors.

sourceAnchors.name: checklist logic outside surgery
sourceAnchors.detail: The source sidecar says the closing chapter centers on practical routine discipline beyond one field.
sourceAnchors.phrasingHint: The form changes when the field changes, but the same human vulnerability is still waiting at the decision point.

counterintuition: The checklist is universal but not identical
tryThisNow: Make a checklist for one decision

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

exampleSpecs.domain: Laura, an investment committee analyst building a decision checklist
exampleSpecs.audience: investors who have enough analysis but repeat the same judgment errors
exampleSpecs.stakes: a tempting acquisition looks cheap while debt covenants and customer concentration repeat a past mistake
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Laura uses the checklist to force covenant, concentration, and downside-case checks before the committee debates upside
exampleSpecs.firstImage: quarterly reports stacked beside a silent speakerphone

exampleSpecs.domain: Julien, a restaurant group owner reviewing expansion
exampleSpecs.audience: operators transferring checklist logic without copying medicine
exampleSpecs.stakes: a second location decision fails if lease excitement hides staffing and supplier weaknesses
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Julien rebuilds the checklist around lease terms, chef bench strength, supplier redundancy, and cash runway instead of borrowing a safety form
exampleSpecs.firstImage: What would be stupid to copy from a hospital checklist into a restaurant lease meeting?

exampleSpecs.domain: Chloe, an independent school safeguarding lead
exampleSpecs.audience: school leaders adapting verification to child safety decisions
exampleSpecs.stakes: a volunteer approval process depends on memory and goodwill across three offices
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chloe turns repeated volunteer approval misses into a safeguarding checklist that verifies background check, contact boundaries, and trip role before assignment
exampleSpecs.firstImage: rain tapping against the glass beside a stack of volunteer badges

exampleSpecs.audience: technical leaders deciding where a routine safeguard can support judgment
exampleSpecs.stakes: containment choices repeat past misses when the team trusts memory during live attack response
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Michael adapts checklist logic to the recurring failure points: isolate host, preserve evidence, notify legal, and confirm backup integrity before restoration
exampleSpecs.firstImage: "Do not restore until we know what we are restoring from," Michael says
mustAvoid: data center live incident card from ch06

exampleSpecs.domain: Catarina, an architecture firm code-review partner
exampleSpecs.audience: professional-service teams who need safeguards without flattening design judgment
exampleSpecs.stakes: a beautiful design repeats a costly accessibility miss from last year
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Catarina builds a code-review checklist only around recurring misses, then leaves aesthetic and site-specific judgment outside the list
exampleSpecs.firstImage: It took Catarina one rejected permit set to stop treating memory as a quality system

exampleSpecs.domain: Chidi, a nonprofit grant approval chair
exampleSpecs.audience: boards deciding whether a checklist fits mission decisions
exampleSpecs.stakes: a beloved project wins approval while conflicts, reporting burden, and reserve risk are missed again
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Chidi limits the checklist to recurring blind spots before the vote and refuses to let it score the mission value itself
exampleSpecs.firstImage: You watch the room lean toward the story before anyone asks about the reserve account

skillTargets: transfer checklist logic without copying form
evaluate when a checklist would become blind procedure

tryThisNowSpec: Pick one recurring decision outside medicine and write the two failure points experience has already shown you, not the whole decision process.

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'
